其散辨分
是言之勢有所必極極則
punctuated: 祖訓，畫一而守之久矣。今更制易法，則有紛亂約束之譏；以義斷恩，則有削疎骨肉之罪；忍而坐視，則蠹耗愈甚，卒有土崩之憂；僅而補緝，則苟幸旦夕，不救衝決之禍。故雖計臣謀士，莫爲破盈庭之言而建必然之畫者，難之也。雖然，釋今弗圖，則後世之難且十百此矣。請試言之。漢初，諸侯王置吏握兵，同制天子，其患在强大而不掉。自武帝推恩分王，則宗室子弟莫不受地矣。然王之庶子間爲列侯，侯之庶子絕無爵土，有去而爲民者，有爲民而復仕于朝者。自是而後，無諸侯王之患，亦無養宗室之費，其經制定也。唐之末也，帝裔王支流播民間，其患在離渙而不屬。自宋養之京師，則五葉之後，騷然煩費矣。其後辨親疎之等，明襲序之法，袒免以下不復賜名，敦宗之院散居郡□□。以宋雖費于前，而大省于後，其救弊果□□是言之，勢有所必極，極則
translation_en:
…the Ancestral Injunctions, whose uniform provisions have long been observed. Now, to alter the institutions and change the laws would invite criticism for throwing established rules into confusion; to curtail benevolence in the name of righteousness would incur the guilt of diminishing and estranging one’s own flesh and blood. Yet to endure the situation and watch idly would allow the drain on resources to worsen, ultimately threatening collapse; merely to patch things up would mean hoping to scrape through from day to day, without averting a disastrous breach. Thus even fiscal officials and advisers have been unable to cut through the court’s profusion of opinions and establish a plan certain to succeed: such is the difficulty. Nevertheless, if we let matters rest now without devising a solution, the difficulties facing later generations will be ten or a hundred times greater. Let me venture to explain.
At the beginning of the Han, the princes appointed officials and commanded troops, enjoying arrangements comparable to those of the Son of Heaven. The danger lay in their being too powerful to control. Once Emperor Wu extended favor by dividing the princely domains, all the sons and younger members of the imperial clan received land. Yet princes’ sons other than their heirs sometimes became marquises, while marquises’ sons other than their heirs received neither titles nor lands. Some left to become commoners; others, having become commoners, subsequently entered service at court. Thereafter there was neither danger from the princes nor the expense of supporting the imperial clan. This was because the enduring institutional arrangements had been settled.
At the end of the Tang, imperial descendants and branches of princely houses were scattered among the common people. The danger lay in their dispersal and loss of connection. When the Song supported them in the capital, after five generations the resulting expense had become a source of commotion. Later, distinctions between nearer and more distant kin were established, and the rules governing the order of succession were clarified. Those related only within the lowest mourning degree, tanwen, or more distantly, were no longer granted personal names by the emperor; those of the Court for Promoting Clan Amity were dispersed among the prefectures [?]. Thus, although the Song incurred expenses earlier, it achieved great savings later; its remedy for these abuses was decisive [?]. Speaking on this basis [?], circumstances must reach an extreme; once that extreme is reached…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
必通恩有所必窮窮則必殺茲非其明效
大驗耶
高皇帝神武開基忠厚立國故利建宗子以疆
本朝明惇睦之誼以先天下然是時宗室之
衆無幾可按籍而數也今熙洽二百餘年
麟趾爪瓞綿昌浩衍麗屬籍者四萬而存
者二萬八千五百有奇以祿計之不下八
九百萬設一傳再傳而後其生齒什倍其
祿又當什倍此勢之所必極而恩之所必
===
窮也故欲竭天下之賦以奉宗室則國益
病裁宗室之祿以紓國計則宗室亦益病
何者今賦斂非減而積貯非盈也乃水旱
爲灾迄無寧歲諸邊轉餉未見休時財力
亦甚詘矣加以宗室之祿日引月長則賦
安得不竭而國安得不病語曰附枝大者
賊本心此善喻也且宗室至貴倨也又非
人人能謀生也今祿既益微罔亦少密業
已困矣而有司奉行條例一切以法繩之

punctuated:
必通；恩有所必窮，窮則必殺。茲非其明效大驗耶？
高皇帝神武開基，忠厚立國，故利建宗子以疆本朝，明惇睦之誼以先天下。然是時宗室之衆無幾，可按籍而數也。今熙洽二百餘年，麟趾爪瓞，綿昌浩衍，麗屬籍者四萬，而存者二萬八千五百有奇。以祿計之，不下八九百萬。設一傳再傳而後，其生齒什倍，其祿又當什倍，此勢之所必極，而恩之所必窮也。故欲竭天下之賦以奉宗室，則國益病；裁宗室之祿以紓國計，則宗室亦益病。何者？今賦斂非減，而積貯非盈也。乃水旱爲灾，迄無寧歲；諸邊轉餉，未見休時。財力亦甚詘矣。加以宗室之祿日引月長，則賦安得不竭，而國安得不病？語曰：「附枝大者賊本心。」此善喻也。且宗室至貴倨也，又非人人能謀生也。今祿既益微，罔亦少密，業已困矣，而有司奉行條例，一切以法繩之，
translation_en:
…must give way to change; beneficence necessarily reaches a point of exhaustion, and when exhausted it must be curtailed. Is this not clear and compelling proof?
Emperor Gao founded the dynasty through divine martial prowess and established the state upon loyalty and generosity. He therefore enfeoffed sons of the imperial clan to strengthen the ruling house, and made manifest the obligations of familial affection and harmony to set an example for all under Heaven. At that time, however, members of the imperial clan were few and could be counted by consulting the registers. Now, after more than two hundred years of peace and harmony, their descendants, like the qilin’s offspring and the spreading gourds [?], have multiplied in abundant succession. Forty thousand are entered in the imperial clan registers, of whom somewhat more than twenty-eight thousand five hundred are living. Their stipends amount to no less than eight or nine million. Suppose that after another generation or two their numbers increase tenfold: their stipends must likewise increase tenfold. This is where circumstances must reach their limit and beneficence must be exhausted. Thus, if all the tax revenues of the realm are exhausted to support the imperial clan, the state becomes still more distressed; if the clan’s stipends are reduced to relieve state finances, the clan likewise becomes still more distressed. Why is this? Tax exactions have not diminished, yet accumulated reserves are not abundant. Floods and droughts bring disaster, with not a single peaceful year, while the transport of provisions to the various frontiers has seen no respite. Financial resources are already severely strained. Add to this the daily and monthly growth of the imperial clan’s stipends: how can revenues fail to be exhausted, and how can the state fail to suffer? As the saying goes, “When attached branches grow too large, they injure the heart of the trunk.” This is an apt analogy. Moreover, members of the imperial clan are exceedingly exalted and haughty, and not all can earn a livelihood. Now their stipends have grown ever smaller, while the net of restrictions has tightened somewhat, leaving them already in hardship. Yet the responsible officials enforce the regulations, holding them in every matter to the law…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
令揺手觸禁資身無策則安所歸命也盖
宗室亦極病巳語曰饑寒切于人之肌膚
欲其毋為奸邪不可得也此非細故也故
雖桑孔握籌晁賈挾策而圖今日之敝終
不能兩利而兼得矣愚故曰勢之所必極
而恩之所必窮胡不引漢唐宋之事以觀
之也夫揚湯止沸無益也不如絶薪止火
而巳子孫而守先人之廬至于棟折榱傾
不得不撤而新之為其將壓也今承
===
祖宗之業視國家之敝不思變通安全之則何
異以指撓沸以繩維顛乎愚以為
祖訓至嚴而善推
聖祖之意則猶繼述也宗室至親而曲體宗室
之情則所以親親也何以言之
國初親王歲祿五萬他賜予甚盛不數歲而
裁為萬石又以民貧賦少給
代肅諸王僅五百石或千石耳夫莫富于海

之也夫揚湯止沸無益也不如絶薪止火

異以指撓沸以繩維顛乎愚以爲
祖訓至嚴而善推
聖祖之意則循繼述也宗室至親而曲體宗室
之情則所以親親也何以言之

令揺手觸禁，資身無策，則安所歸命也？盖宗室亦極病巳。語曰：「饑寒切于人之肌膚，欲其毋為奸邪，不可得也。」此非細故也。故雖桑孔握籌，晁賈挾策，而圖今日之敝，終不能兩利而兼得矣。愚故曰：勢之所必極，而恩之所必窮。胡不引漢唐宋之事以觀之也？夫揚湯止沸，無益也，不如絶薪止火而巳。子孫而守先人之廬，至于棟折榱傾，不得不撤而新之，為其將壓也。今承祖宗之業，視國家之敝，不思變通安全之，則何異以指撓沸，以繩維顛乎？

愚以為祖訓至嚴，而善推聖祖之意，則猶繼述也；宗室至親，而曲體宗室之情，則所以親親也。何以言之？國初親王歲祿五萬，他賜予甚盛，不數歲而裁為萬石。又以民貧賦少，給代肅諸王僅五百石或千石耳。夫莫富于海內，莫親于天子之子，不加賦而奪之祿者
translation_en:
…so that they encounter a prohibition whenever they so much as move a hand, and have no means of supporting themselves—where, then, can they turn to preserve their lives? The imperial clansmen, too, are already in extreme distress. As the saying goes: “When hunger and cold bite into people's flesh, it is impossible to expect them to refrain from wrongdoing.” This is no minor matter. Thus, even if Sang and Kong wielded the counting rods, and Chao and Jia brought forward their plans to remedy today's abuses, they could never secure the interests of both sides at once. Hence my humble contention: circumstances must eventually reach their limit, and imperial bounty must eventually be exhausted. Why not examine the precedents of the Han, Tang, and Song? Lifting hot water to stop it boiling is useless; better simply to cut off the fuel and extinguish the fire. When descendants preserve their forebears' dwelling, but its beams break and its rafters lean, they have no choice but to dismantle and rebuild it, lest it collapse upon them. Now, having inherited the enterprise of the imperial ancestors, if we observe the troubles of the state yet give no thought to adapting its arrangements to secure its safety, how is this different from stirring boiling water with a finger or trying to hold up a collapsing structure with a rope?

In my humble view, although the Ancestral Injunctions are supremely strict, properly extending the intentions of the sagely founder is still to carry on his work. Although the imperial clansmen are the closest of kin, attending sensitively to their circumstances is precisely how one shows affection for one's kin. Why do I say this? At the beginning of the dynasty, the annual stipend of an imperial prince was fifty thousand shi of grain, and other gifts were exceedingly lavish. Within a few years, however, the stipend was reduced to ten thousand shi. Moreover, because the people were poor and tax revenues scant, the princes of Dai, Su, and other princedoms were granted only five hundred or one thousand shi. Nothing is richer than the realm, and no kinship is closer than that of the Son of Heaven's sons; yet the reason for reducing their stipends instead of increasing taxation was…

也
祖訓言將軍以下有材能者得改官陞轉如銓
選法夫既富貴之矣猶不絕其仕進者所
以興其善行而消其怙侈使外有親賢之

趨富厚而逃貧困然今予之虛名而奪之

未有莫爲之限制而能世世無弊者也古
punctuated:
以為寧儉宗室□□以耗國計、疲民力也。

祖訓言：「將軍以下有材能者，得改官陞轉，如銓選法。」夫既富貴之矣，猶不絕其仕進者，所以興其善行而消其怙侈，使外有親賢之重，而內有省費之利也。然則聖祖之意可推也。人情孰不欲生全而惡危亡，趨富厚而逃貧困？然今予之虛名而奪之實惠，則三尺童子不願有矣。曩者宗室獻議，有請試官自效者，有請力田自給者。夫田農至拙業也，簿書之吏至詘體也，猶願為之。彼擁有爵之虛名，而棄資生之實惠，其情固弗樂也。然則宗室之情可察也。

今欲善推聖祖之意，而曲體宗室之情，其當議者有三：以正倫分，則封爵當議；以廣德厚，則禁例當議；以節浮冗，則恩數當議。何者？天下之法，未有莫為之限制而能世世無弊者也。古
translation_en:
…because he considered it preferable to impose frugality upon the imperial clan [two illegible characters; the connection is uncertain] rather than deplete the resources of the state and exhaust the strength of the people [?].

The Ancestral Instructions state: “Those holding the rank of General or below who possess talent and ability may transfer to other offices and receive promotion in accordance with the rules governing official selection.” Although he had already granted them wealth and honor, he did not close off their advancement in official service. This was intended to encourage their good conduct and dispel their reliance on privilege and their extravagance, thereby outwardly securing the esteem that comes from cherishing kinsmen and worthy men, while inwardly obtaining the benefit of reduced expenditure. Thus the intentions of the Sagely Ancestor can be inferred. Who, by human nature, does not desire survival and safety and loathe danger and destruction, seek wealth and abundance and flee poverty and hardship? Yet if we now give them empty titles while depriving them of tangible benefits, even a small child would not wish to possess them. Previously, members of the imperial clan submitted proposals: some requested permission to serve provisionally in office and demonstrate their usefulness; others requested permission to support themselves by farming. Farming is the humblest of occupations, and serving as a clerk handling registers and documents is profoundly demeaning to one’s status; nevertheless, they were willing to do these things. To possess the empty distinction of noble rank while foregoing the tangible means of sustaining life is certainly not something they welcome. Thus the feelings of the imperial clan can be understood.

If we now wish properly to carry forward the intentions of the Sagely Ancestor and sympathetically comprehend the circumstances of the imperial clan, three matters require deliberation. To rectify distinctions of kinship and status, we must deliberate on the conferral of noble ranks; to extend generous beneficence, we must deliberate on the prohibitory regulations; to curtail superfluous expenditure, we must deliberate on the scale of imperial favors. Why is this? No institution in the world can remain free from abuses for generation after generation without limits being imposed upon it. In antiquity…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
者五世袒免六世而親屬絕至于祖宗之
廟猶限之以七世親盡而迭毁今已絕之
屬猶儕于五服之親則無等也忍于親盡
之祖而不忍于親盡之子孫則舛也誠宜
按諸屬籍別其世次而為之限制如
親王世及矣其次封郡王者可限也郡王世
襲矣其次封鎮國將軍者可限也諸將軍
中尉以嫡相繼矣其一子降封之外可已
也奉國中尉一子得襲矣其世世承襲之
===
例可已也大抵以位尊卑為之多寡以世
親疎為之隆殺其不得封者皆如漢列侯
庶子之法則坐食可益省而詔祿可繼此
封爵之當議者也古者公族得仕于朝非
絕之也庶民之家得占田治生非禁之也
今宗室特以例見疑是以賢愚同滯而人
無聊生矣夫既限以封爵則絕封之始宜
人予之貲賦之間田以為永業令家自為
養而盡弛出城諸禁其材者得應舉試外

===

絕之也庶民之家得占田治生非禁之也
今宗室將以例見疑是以賢愚同滯而人
無聊生矣夫既限以封爵則絕封之始宜
人予之貲賦之閒田以爲永業令家自爲
養而盡弛出城諸禁其材者得應舉試外
punctuated:
者，五世袒免，六世而親屬絕。至于祖宗之廟，猶限之以七世，親盡而迭毁。今已絕之屬，猶儕于五服之親，則無等也；忍于親盡之祖，而不忍于親盡之子孫，則舛也。誠宜按諸屬籍，別其世次，而為之限制。如親王世及矣，其次封郡王者可限也；郡王世襲矣，其次封鎮國將軍者可限也；諸將軍、中尉以嫡相繼矣，其一子降封之外可已也；奉國中尉一子得襲矣，其世世承襲之例可已也。大抵以位尊卑為之多寡，以世親疎為之隆殺。其不得封者，皆如漢列侯庶子之法，則坐食可益省，而詔祿可繼。此封爵之當議者也。

古者公族得仕于朝，非絕之也；庶民之家得占田治生，非禁之也。今宗室特以例見疑，是以賢愚同滯，而人無聊生矣。夫既限以封爵，則絕封之始，宜人予之貲，賦之間田，以為永業，令家自為養，而盡弛出城諸禁。其材者得應舉試外
translation_en:
…in antiquity, relatives in the fifth generation observed the mourning rite of baring the arm and wearing a mourning headband; by the sixth generation, the kinship obligation ended. Even the ancestral temples were limited to seven generations: when the kinship obligation expired, the shrines were dismantled in succession. Yet today, relatives whose kinship obligations have already ended are still ranked alongside relatives within the five degrees of mourning. This allows no distinctions. To bear ending such observances for ancestors beyond the prescribed degree of kinship, yet be unable to do so for their descendants, is inconsistent. We should indeed consult the registers of the imperial clan, distinguish their generations, and establish limits. For example, princes already transmit their titles from generation to generation; grants of the next rank, commandery prince, to their other descendants can be limited. Commandery princes already enjoy hereditary succession; grants of the next rank, Bulwark General, to their other descendants can be limited. The various generals and commandants already transmit their titles through the principal line; apart from granting a reduced title to one son, further grants can cease. One son of a Commandant Who Supports the State already has the right of succession; the rule permitting this succession to continue generation after generation can be abolished. In general, the number of grants should vary with the rank’s standing, and their generosity should vary with generational proximity. Those who receive no title should all be treated according to the Han rules for the sons of ranked marquises other than their principal heirs. Then the number maintained without working can be further reduced, and imperially granted stipends [?] can be sustained. These are the matters concerning the granting of titles that should be deliberated.

In antiquity, members of the ruling lineage could serve at court; they were not excluded. Commoner households could hold land and earn their livelihoods; they were not prohibited from doing so. Today, members of the imperial clan are treated with suspicion solely because of established regulations. Consequently, worthy and foolish alike are held back, and people have no means of livelihood. Once limits have been placed on the granting of titles, those whose entitlement to a title first ends should each receive funds and an allotment of vacant land as a permanent holding. Each household should be required to support itself, and all prohibitions on leaving the city should be lifted. Those with ability should be allowed to sit for the examinations and be tried in service outside…

text:
官如常法或擢□□□□見如蘇轍所謂臨
以按察持以寮□□□以刑禁使不材者不
至害民賢者有以自效顧不可乎此禁例
之當議者也且夫禮所以爲節而法所以
爲懲今罪庶人有給已猶無罪也已罪黜
而猶給之與詔祿無別非所以爲懲也自
郡主至鄕君有祿已猶同姓也至諸儀賓

軍中尉之限祿皆半給餘皆量給婚資則

者也如是則可以清蠹耗之原紓待哺之

translation_en:
…serve in offices outside the capital under the ordinary rules, or be promoted [four illegible characters] [?]. As Su Zhe put it, “Supervise them through surveillance officials, restrain them through colleagues [three illegible characters] and penal prohibitions” [?]. Thus the incapable would not come to harm the people, while the worthy would have a means to demonstrate their abilities. Surely this would be possible? These are the prohibitory regulations that ought to be reconsidered.

Ritual provides restraint, while law provides punishment. At present, offenders reduced to commoner status receive allowances just as though they had committed no offense [?]. To continue supporting them after they have been punished and stripped of rank, without distinguishing this from stipends granted by imperial decree, does not serve the purpose of punishment. Those from Commandery Princess down to Township Lady receive stipends, but they are, after all, of the imperial surname. As for the Ceremonial Consorts, marriage into the princely houses already gives them honor and standing. Failing to reduce their stipends does not serve the purpose of restraint.

In my humble view, all those demoted to commoner status should be governed by the same rules as commoners whose hereditary enfeoffment has ceased. Commandery Princesses should follow the limits established for Commandery Princes; County Princesses and those below them should follow the limits established for Generals and Commandants. Their stipends should all be paid at half rate, while the remainder should receive only appropriately assessed marriage allowances. Imperial beneficence would then not be claimed improperly or bestowed excessively, and expenditure would certainly be greatly reduced. These are the provisions for imperial favors that ought to be reconsidered.

In this way, the sources of wasteful depletion could be eliminated and the distress of those awaiting sustenance relieved. Above, the profound intentions of the sagely founding emperor would be preserved; below, the circumstances and feelings of the imperial clan would be accommodated. Such is the broad outline.

Yet I have heard that those who remedy abuses must return to their origins, and those who reform institutions must anticipate the eventual consequences. Once limits are placed on enfeoffment, might some not become resentful and raise a collective outcry? Once the prohibitory regulations are relaxed, might some not act recklessly and commit violence?…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
恩數節矣得無有顛連而失所者乎則愚
又以為盈縮之議在下而操縱之機在上惟
聖天子燭安危之故恢繼述之圖毅然獨斷而
力行之示
諸王以大義不得不通之法則必有河間東
平之賢奉宣德意而深樂其便者何至于
羣譁有爵者制之于王國絕封者治之以
有司何患乎為暴且齊民非廩于官而固
有比于封君者宗室而有永業世世無有
===
所與設
天子不忘恩厚舉古賜民粟帛之令以間恤之
何憂乎失所較之歲祿不給而羣辱有司
犯禁而不止救死而不贍者利害相百也
此之不為而顧彼之久行至于勢不可復
反恩無所復施則其害不獨宗室且移之
社稷矣故為之于可為則易為之于不可
為則難今
天子仁明英斷釐弊剔蠹以興至理賢公卿能

羣譁有爵者制之于王國絶封者治之以
有司何患乎爲暴且齊民非廩于官而固
有比于封君者宗室而有永業世世無有
===
天子不忘恩厚舉古賜民粟帛之令以閒恤之
何憂乎失所較之歲祿不給而羣辱有司
犯禁而不止救死而不贍者利害相百也
此之不爲而顧彼之久行至于勢不可復
反恩無所復施則其害不獨宗室且移之
社稷矣故爲之于可爲則易爲之于不可
爲則難今
天子仁明英斷釐弊剔蠹以興至理賢公卿能
所與謀
punctuated: 恩數節矣，得無有顛連而失所者乎？則愚又以為，盈縮之議在下，而操縱之機在上。惟聖天子燭安危之故，恢繼述之圖，毅然獨斷而力行之，示諸王以大義、不得不通之法，則必有河間、東平之賢，奉宣德意而深樂其便者，何至于羣譁？有爵者制之于王國，絕封者治之以有司，何患乎為暴？且齊民非廩于官，而固有比于封君者。宗室而有永業，世世無有所與，設天子不忘恩厚，舉古賜民粟帛之令，以間恤之，何憂乎失所？較之歲祿不給而羣辱有司，犯禁而不止，救死而不贍者，利害相百也。此之不為，而顧彼之久行，至于勢不可復反，恩無所復施，則其害不獨宗室，且移之社稷矣。故為之于可為則易，為之于不可為則難。今天子仁明英斷，釐弊剔蠹，以興至理，賢公卿能
translation_en:
…Once imperial benefactions are curtailed, might some not fall into distress and lose their means of support? I further believe that proposals for increasing or reducing provision belong to those below, while the power to tighten or relax control rests with the sovereign above. If only the sage Son of Heaven would discern the causes of security and danger, enlarge his plans for carrying forward his predecessors’ work, and resolutely decide and vigorously implement these measures, showing the princes the greater moral obligation and the regulations that must be adapted, there would surely be worthy men like the princes of Hejian and Dongping who would proclaim his benevolent intentions and warmly welcome the advantages. How could this lead to a general outcry? Those holding noble titles would be restrained within their princely establishments; those whose enfeoffment had ceased would be governed by the responsible officials. Why fear that they would commit violence?

Moreover, ordinary subjects receive no government maintenance, yet some certainly possess wealth comparable to that of enfeoffed lords. If members of the imperial clan had permanent estates, with no interference for generations [?], and if the Son of Heaven, mindful of his generous favor, invoked the ancient ordinances for granting grain and silk to the people and offered them occasional relief, why worry that they would lose their means of support? Compared with the present situation, in which annual stipends go unpaid, clan members collectively subject officials to indignities, violations of prohibitions continue unchecked, and assistance is insufficient to save people from death, the balance of benefit and harm would differ a hundredfold.

If these measures are not undertaken, and the existing practices are instead allowed to persist until the situation can no longer be reversed and imperial kindness can no longer be bestowed, the harm will affect not only the imperial clan but also the state itself. Thus, acting while action remains possible is easy; acting when it has become impossible is difficult. Today the Son of Heaven is humane, discerning, and decisively resolute; he corrects abuses and removes sources of corruption to bring about the finest governance. The worthy dukes and ministers can…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
矢謨陳力爲國家任大事以圖大功則何
有于草野之言哉姑以復明問云爾
第四問
郭子章
同考試官教諭王批品題古今人物鑿鑿詳
確以誠與才立論尤見古今聞望本原觀此作𠞰其名世之英耶
同考試官學正段批古今豪傑樹勲揚名誠
與才耳是作闡發詳悉且評品低昻洞有酌見可以占所養矣
同考試官進士孫批古今人物敷對詳明誠
===
與才合尤爲知本且其間條陳敘述俱出入史典于其聞望之
表表者歟
考試官修撰申批揚扠古今品藻允當而慷慨自許
於言外見之必佳士也宜錄
考試官右諭德丁批品隲前修析如指掌多識畜德之
士也取之
古今人臣所以繫天下之望者其惟誠與
才合乎是故忠信篤敬履正不渝者其誠
也訏謨大畧應變不窮者其才也惟誠也

郭子章

同考試官教諭王批：品題古今人物，鑿鑿詳確，以誠與才立論，尤見古今聞望本原。觀此作，𠞰其名世之英耶？

同考試官學正段批：古今豪傑樹勲揚名，誠與才耳。是作闡發詳悉，且評品低昻，洞有酌見，可以占所養矣。

同考試官進士孫批：古今人物，敷對詳明，誠與才合，尤爲知本。且其間條陳敘述，俱出入史典，于其聞望之表表者歟？

考試官修撰申批：揚扠古今，品藻允當，而慷慨自許，於言外見之，必佳士也，宜錄。

古今人臣所以繫天下之望者，其惟誠與才合乎？是故忠信篤敬、履正不渝者，其誠也；訏謨大畧、應變不窮者，其才也。惟誠也
translation_en:
…set forth their plans and exert their strength, undertaking great affairs for the state in pursuit of great achievements—what need, then, have they of the words of a man outside official life? I offer these merely in reply to your enlightened question.

Fourth Policy Question
Guo Zizhang

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: His assessments of figures past and present are precise, detailed, and sound. By grounding his argument in sincerity and ability, he particularly reveals the source of their renown and prestige throughout history. Judging from this composition, might he be an outstanding talent who will win fame in his age [?]?

Comment by Associate Examiner Duan, School Director: The heroes of past and present have established achievements and won fame through sincerity and ability alone. This composition expounds these qualities fully and in detail. Moreover, its rankings and appraisals display penetrating and considered judgment, allowing us to discern the cultivation of its author.

Comment by Associate Examiner Sun, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi): His discussion of figures past and present is detailed and clear. In joining sincerity with ability, he shows particular understanding of the fundamentals. Furthermore, his systematic exposition and narrative throughout draw freely upon the historical classics. Might he be among those outstanding in renown and prestige [?]?

Comment by Examiner Shen, Senior Compiler: He surveys [?] past and present, and his appraisals are just. A spirited confidence in his own aspirations is evident beyond his words. He must be a worthy scholar and should be selected.

Comment by Examiner Ding, Right Admonisher: He appraises worthy predecessors and analyzes them as clearly as if pointing to the palm of his hand. He is a scholar of broad learning and cultivated virtue. Accept him.

Is it not precisely the union of sincerity and ability that enables ministers, past and present, to command the hopes of all under Heaven? Thus, loyalty, trustworthiness, earnestness, reverence, and an unwavering adherence to upright conduct constitute their sincerity; far-reaching counsel, grand strategies, and an inexhaustible capacity to respond to changing circumstances constitute their ability. It is precisely through sincerity…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
故能通天下之志惟才也故能成天下之
務修此二者而天下之望歸焉矣古之人
臣所以垂休光照後世負天下之望而爲
之前者此也今之人臣所以享大名顯當
世負天下之望而爲之後者亦此也明於
此則可以上下前修權衡人物矣粤昔三
五之世光嶽氣完名世輩出當其時百僚
師師百官濟濟不可尚已非無聞望也人
人而有之也譬則繁星麗空孰闚五緯之
===
耀芒哉三代以還醇朴日散名世罕生當
其時爲□爲蜮淟涊依阿風斯下矣非始
有聞望也絕無而僅有也譬則晨星相望
𤍠然而見者不曰維參與昴哉兹即執事
所舉者言之以直諫顯而寢强藩之謀者
非汲長孺乎以義槩著而忤姦雄之心者
非孔文舉乎夫淮南驕蹇逆節之萌非一
日也長孺以直言敢諫之氣潜銷其無將
倍畔之謀何其偉哉然義形于色不直淮

punctuated: 故能通天下之志；惟才也，故能成天下之務。修此二者，而天下之望歸焉矣。古之人臣所以垂休光、照後世，負天下之望而爲之前者，此也；今之人臣所以享大名、顯當世，負天下之望而爲之後者，亦此也。明於此，則可以上下前修、權衡人物矣。粤昔三五之世，光嶽氣完，名世輩出。當其時，百僚師師，百官濟濟，不可尚已。非無聞望也，人人而有之也。譬則繁星麗空，孰闚五緯之耀芒哉？三代以還，醇朴日散，名世罕生。當其時，爲□爲蜮，淟涊依阿，風斯下矣。非始有聞望也，絕無而僅有也。譬則晨星相望，𤍠然而見者，不曰維參與昴哉？兹即執事所舉者言之，以直諫顯而寢强藩之謀者，非汲長孺乎？以義槩著而忤姦雄之心者，非孔文舉乎？夫淮南驕蹇，逆節之萌非一日也。長孺以直言敢諫之氣，潜銷其無將倍畔之謀，何其偉哉！然義形于色，不直淮
translation_en:
…and thus can comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven; it is talent that enables one to accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven. Cultivate these two qualities, and the hopes of the realm will converge upon you. These were what enabled ministers of antiquity to leave a glorious legacy illuminating later generations, bearing the hopes of the realm as their predecessors; these likewise enable ministers today to enjoy great renown and distinction in their own age, bearing the hopes of the realm as their successors. Understanding this, one can rank the worthy predecessors and weigh the merits of men.

In the distant age of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the vital force of Heaven and the sacred mountains remained whole, and men renowned in their age arose in succession. Officials emulated one another, and the ranks of office were filled with worthy men: nothing could surpass them. It was not that reputation and prestige were absent; everyone possessed them. It was like a multitude of stars arrayed across the sky: who could distinguish the radiance of the five planets? Since the Three Dynasties, unspoiled integrity has dissipated day by day, and men renowned in their age have rarely appeared. Men acted as □ [?] and as malevolent sprites, sullied themselves, and compliantly followed others; prevailing conduct thus declined. It was not that reputation and prestige first appeared then, but that scarcely anyone possessed them, save a very few. It was like the scattered stars at dawn: would not those still conspicuously visible [?] be Shen and Mao?

Now, to speak of the men you have cited: was it not Ji Changru who became distinguished for forthright remonstrance and brought a powerful feudatory prince’s schemes to rest? Was it not Kong Wenju who became renowned for righteous integrity and thwarted the ambitions of an unscrupulous strongman? The prince of Huainan was arrogant and unruly; the seeds of his rebellion had been growing for more than a day. Through his spirit of frank speech and fearless remonstrance, Changru quietly dissolved the prince’s incipient designs for treason and rebellion. How admirable he was! Yet righteousness showed in his countenance, and it was not only Huai…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
南畏之不冠不見武帝亦憚之矣所謂社
稷之臣與曹瞞蓄異雄心之逞亦非一日
也文舉以高志直情之風默奪其僭擬無
涯之念何其壯哉雖子丕代終之覬卒成
於身後而老瞞移鼎之迹竟隔于人存也
所謂秋霜比質與皆望隆于漢者也單騎
免胄下回紇之拜者非郭子儀乎推赤去
備安反側之心者非裴中立乎夫吐蕃內
寇涇陽被圍王室誠岌岌也單騎免胄若
===
示怯矣卒之羶裘革面能致回紇之拜馬
是豈計數所能及哉盖其忠義相勉騰茂
有年推轂之初人已有失亡著者若子儀
者其真神明扶持者與身親督戰淮蔡甫
平人心尚洶洶也推心示赤若無備矣卒
之蔡人感泣能安反側之心焉是豈權詐
所能與哉盖其以死自誓決策已堅持節
之始已有奪其心者若中立者其真至誠
動物者與皆望隆於唐者也乃若出領延

punctuated:
南畏之，不冠不見，武帝亦憚之矣。所謂社稷之臣與！曹瞞蓄異，雄心之逞亦非一日也。文舉以高志直情之風，默奪其僭擬無涯之念，何其壯哉！雖子丕代終之覬卒成於身後，而老瞞移鼎之迹竟隔于人存也。所謂秋霜比質與！皆望隆于漢者也。
單騎免胄，下回紇之拜者，非郭子儀乎？推赤去備，安反側之心者，非裴中立乎？夫吐蕃內寇，涇陽被圍，王室誠岌岌也。單騎免胄，若示怯矣；卒之羶裘革面，能致回紇之拜馬，是豈計數所能及哉？盖其忠義相勉，騰茂有年，推轂之初，人已有失亡著者。若子儀者，其真神明扶持者與！身親督戰，淮蔡甫平，人心尚洶洶也。推心示赤，若無備矣；卒之蔡人感泣，能安反側之心焉，是豈權詐所能與哉？盖其以死自誓，決策已堅，持節之始，已有奪其心者。若中立者，其真至誠動物者與！皆望隆於唐者也。
乃若出領延
translation_en:
…Huainan feared him; Emperor Wu too stood in awe of him and would not receive him without wearing his cap. Was he not what is called a minister who safeguards the altars of soil and grain! Cao Man had harbored treasonous designs and indulged his overweening ambitions for more than a single day. Through his lofty aspirations and forthright disposition, Wenju quietly checked Cao’s boundless desire to usurp imperial standing. How magnificent! Although Cao’s son Pi eventually fulfilled his ambition to replace the dynasty after Wenju’s death, old Cao Man’s steps toward seizing the throne remained blocked while Wenju lived. Was he not one whose character could be compared to autumn frost! These were men of towering prestige under the Han.
Was it not Guo Ziyi who rode out alone, removed his helmet, and brought the Huihe to bow before him? Was it not Pei Zhongli who displayed his sincerity, dispensed with precautions, and calmed the hearts of the wavering? When the Tufan invaded and Jingyang was besieged, the imperial house was indeed in grave peril. Riding out alone and removing his helmet might have seemed a display of weakness. Yet in the end those clad in rank-smelling furs changed their outward demeanor, and he secured the submission of the Huihe [the following character, 馬, is doubtful]. How could mere calculation have achieved this? His loyalty and righteousness had encouraged others and flourished for years; at the outset of his appointment to command, people already showed signs of loss [?]. Was not a man like Ziyi truly sustained by the spirits!
He personally supervised the fighting; Huai and Cai had only just been pacified, and people’s hearts were still deeply unsettled. To open his heart and display his sincerity might have seemed to leave him unguarded. Yet in the end the people of Cai wept with gratitude, and he calmed the hearts of the wavering. How could manipulation and deceit compare with this? He had pledged himself even unto death, and his resolve was already firm. From the moment he took up the envoy’s tally of authority, he had already won over their hearts. Was not a man like Zhongli truly able to move others through utter sincerity! These were men of towering prestige under the Tang.
As for the man who went out to take charge of Yan…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
安而夏人相戒無以延州爲意者范仲淹
也入相天子而遼人相敕慎勿生事邊陲
者司馬君實也二臣何修而得此耶蓋小
范之數萬甲兵西人之喪膽也已久司馬
之忠亮夙著夷虜之知慕也尤深否則以
爲可取而玩之矣惡能致其戒飭如此哉
官居鼎鼐北使至勤咨問者萊公寇準也
再蒞大名虜使不敢褻見者沂公王曾也
二臣何修而得此耶蓋萊公之德望不惟
===
北使知之也而北門鎖鑰自許已高沂公
之治政不惟虜使畏之也而正色立朝時
倚爲重否則以爲易與而侮之矣惡能致
其敬畏如是哉皆望隆于宋者也皆所謂
傑然者也何莫而非誠與才合哉惟我
國家振起人文登延譽望士之乘時崛發者
誠炳炳焉烺烺焉有更僕未易數者至如
執事之所舉者愚生常論其世焉昔也先
犯順事變危疑矣維時內固

再蒞大名虜使不敢褻見者沂公王曾也
二臣何修而得此耶蓋萊公之德望不惟
===

其敬畏如是哉皆望隆于宋者也皆所謂
傑然者也何莫而非誠與才合哉惟我

…[Yan]’an: the man whose appointment there led the people of Xia to warn one another, “Do not entertain designs on Yanzhou,” was Fan Zhongyan. The man whose entry into office as chief minister to the Son of Heaven led the people of Liao to admonish one another, “Take care not to provoke trouble on the frontier,” was Sima Junshi. What had these two ministers cultivated to achieve this? The tens of thousands of armored troops attributed to “Young Fan” had long struck terror into the westerners; Sima’s loyalty and integrity had long been manifest, and the foreign peoples’ recognition and admiration of him were especially deep. Otherwise, they would have considered these men vulnerable and treated them lightly. How could they have been induced to issue such warnings and injunctions?
The man who occupied the chief minister’s seat and about whom arriving northern envoys persistently inquired was Kou Zhun, Duke of Lai. The man who governed Daming a second time, before whom foreign envoys dared not appear disrespectfully, was Wang Zeng, Duke of Yi. What had these two ministers cultivated to achieve this? The Duke of Lai’s virtue and prestige were not merely known to the northern envoys: his own claim to be the “lock and key of the northern gate” already expressed a lofty ambition. The Duke of Yi’s administration was not merely feared by foreign envoys: standing in court with a stern countenance, he was relied upon in his day as a pillar of authority. Otherwise, they would have considered these men easy to deal with and insulted them. How could they have been induced to show such reverence and fear? These were all men of great prestige under the Song, all men who may be called outstanding. In which of them was sincerity not joined with ability?
Our own dynasty has invigorated cultural accomplishment and promoted and welcomed men of renown. Those scholars who have risen to prominence as their times afforded opportunity are truly brilliant and radiant; even with successive attendants taking turns, one could not readily finish counting them. title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
京師外籌邊鎮則于肅愍之功爲烈也
英皇復辟日月重光矣維時引用忠良奠安國
本則李文達之力居多也一則主上推誠
大璫敬憚一則密勿帷幄人望如神聞望
何隆耶哈密之失守禍變未有已也而指
授方畧計襲牙蘭非馬端肅之奇策乎朝
鮮之請道倉猝至難斷也而力沮其議先
人伐謀非劉忠宣之遠猷乎一則威聲大
振西域以寧一則防患未然國是以定其
===
聞望何隆耶至若貢夷之驕詐未有能約
束之者而戢戢聽命韜弓斂矢何謀以致
之耶則以戎政克修嚴爲節制許襄毅得
制禦之本耳是以威名遠播瓦剌輸琛可
不謂大畧哉榆林之經始未爲重鎮也而
嚙指相顧不敢鳴鏑何謀以致之耶則以
因戍置伍拓地列屯余肅敏得經畧之宜
耳是以巨鎮巍然西夷駭愕可不謂膚功
哉之六臣者常變雖殊其遭而剛大之操

…the capital, while planning for the frontier garrisons beyond it: here Yu Sumin’s (于肅愍) achievement was outstanding. When Emperor Yingzong regained the throne, the sun and moon shone brightly once more. In those circumstances, the greatest share of the credit for bringing loyal and worthy men into service and securing the foundations of the state belonged to Li Wenda (李文達). The former enjoyed his sovereign’s wholehearted trust, while the powerful eunuchs respected and feared him; the latter labored diligently in the inner councils, and people looked up to him as though he were a deity. How exalted were their reputations!

After Hami fell, calamities and upheavals showed no sign of ending. Was it not Ma Duansu’s (馬端肅) extraordinary strategy that furnished the plans and devised the surprise attack on Yalan? When Joseon requested passage, the suddenness of the affair made a decision exceedingly difficult. Was it not Liu Zhongxuan’s (劉忠宣) far-sighted planning that vigorously opposed the proposal and forestalled the other party’s designs? The former’s martial prestige rose greatly, bringing peace to the Western Regions; the latter prevented trouble before it arose, thereby settling the policy of the state. How exalted were their reputations!

As for the arrogance and deceit of the tribute-bearing foreigners, no one had been able to restrain them. Yet they came to obey submissively, putting away their bows and gathering up their arrows. What strategy brought this about? By putting military administration in good order and imposing strict discipline, Xu Xiangyi (許襄毅) grasped the essentials of controlling them. Thus his formidable reputation spread afar, and the Wala offered precious tribute. Can this not be called grand strategy?

When Yulin was first established, it was not yet a major military stronghold. Yet the enemy looked at one another in alarm, biting their fingers, and dared not loose a whistling arrow. What strategy brought this about? By organizing units around the existing garrison, extending the territory, and establishing military colonies, Yu Sumin (余肅敏) found the appropriate means of managing the frontier. Thus a great stronghold stood imposing, and the western foreigners were struck with terror. Can this not be called a magnificent achievement?

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
皆足以塞兩間而不禦先後雖異其軌而
忠貞之績皆足以闗百世而不慚語其剛
直謂爲漢之長孺可也而文舉不足言矣
語其誠信謂爲唐之汾陽可也而晋公當
伯仲矣語其公忠清亮謂爲宋之仲淹宋
之君實可也而萊公沂公可方駕矣孰謂
古今人不相及哉愚生猶有說焉盖聞名
世之作也參天地之化闗盛衰之運其生
也有自來其出也有所爲非偶爾也名世
===
者之立朝也舉動足以繫天下之安危謨
謀足以繫生民之休戚在朝廷則朝廷重
奸邪欺負視之以作止其情在邊疆則邊
疆重四夷八蠻窺之以向背其化非齪齪
者也然亦莫非誠與才合以爲之本者故
漢唐宋諸臣誠與才合是以流徽稱於前
代
國朝諸臣誠與才合是以樹丰采於當年要
之同此心術則同此事功同此事功則同

皆足以塞兩間而不禦，先後雖異其軌，而忠貞之績皆足以闗百世而不慚。語其剛直，謂爲漢之長孺可也，而文舉不足言矣；語其誠信，謂爲唐之汾陽可也，而晋公當伯仲矣；語其公忠清亮，謂爲宋之仲淹、宋之君實可也，而萊公、沂公可方駕矣。孰謂古今人不相及哉？
愚生猶有說焉。盖聞名世之作也，參天地之化，闗盛衰之運。其生也有自來，其出也有所爲，非偶爾也。名世者之立朝也，舉動足以繫天下之安危，謨謀足以繫生民之休戚。在朝廷則朝廷重，奸邪欺負視之以作止其情；在邊疆則邊疆重，四夷八蠻窺之以向背其化，非齪齪者也。然亦莫非誠與才合以爲之本者。故漢唐宋諸臣誠與才合，是以流徽稱於前代；國朝諸臣誠與才合，是以樹丰采於當年。要之，同此心術，則同此事功；同此事功，則同
translation_en:
…all were sufficient to fill the space between Heaven and Earth, unimpeded. Though their paths differed as they came earlier or later, their achievements in loyalty and constancy were all sufficient to stand through a hundred generations without shame. In firmness and uprightness, they may be called the Changru of the Han, while Wenju scarcely merits mention beside them. In sincerity and trustworthiness, they may be called the Fenyang of the Tang, while the Duke of Jin would rank alongside them. In public devotion, loyalty, purity, and integrity, they may be called the Zhongyan and Junshi of the Song, while the Duke of Lai and the Duke of Yi could drive abreast of them. Who says that men of the present cannot measure up to men of antiquity?
I, an unworthy student, have something further to say. I have heard that the rise of men renowned in their age participates in the transforming work of Heaven and Earth and bears upon the course of flourishing and decline. Their birth has its source; their emergence has its purpose. It is no mere accident. When such men serve at court, their actions determine the security or peril of the realm, and their deliberations determine the well-being or suffering of the people. At court, they lend weight to the court: the treacherous, wicked, and deceitful watch them before deciding whether to pursue or restrain their designs. On the frontier, they lend weight to the frontier: the peoples of the four quarters and the eight barbarian regions observe them before accepting or rejecting their civilizing influence. These are no petty, narrow-minded men. Yet in every case, the foundation is the union of sincerity and ability. Thus the ministers of the Han, Tang, and Song united sincerity with ability and thereby left illustrious reputations from earlier dynasties; the ministers of our dynasty united sincerity with ability and thereby established their distinguished bearing in their own day. Essentially, the same disposition of mind produces the same achievements; the same achievements produce the same…

…such exceptional men; one certainly cannot rank them above or below one another. In my humble view, the men of former times resembled the men of antiquity: their sincerity and talent were the same. Thus men of today resemble those of former times: their sincerity and talent are likewise the same. Now the northern barbarians draw their bows in the northern deserts, while the Japanese raiders in the south brandish clubs beside the pools—these are no trifling troubles. 國是

羣疑歷歷指掌博聞遠識非淺學可到宜録以式

京營之制下詢承學豈以芻蕘之鄙亦有與
聞
廟堂之大計者乎愚非其人也夫禮有五經
莫重於祭祭之爲義大矣而考訂從祀尤
祀典之重者也可輕議哉天生五材誰能
punctuated:
識不凡，至以祀事宗宋濂之議，戎事遵我世宗之詔，尤爲獨得之見。子於文事武備，盖嘗究心者耶？取之，必有用之才也。
同考試官進士劉批：祀典戎政，係國家大事，不可不講。塲中士子類拾陳言，殊無定見，惟子考稽詳明，折衷曲當，盖經濟之長才，非騁辭華者比也。録之以獻，用定國是。

translation_en:
…His discernment is exceptional. In particular, his adherence to Song Lian’s proposals on sacrificial matters and to the edict of our Emperor Shizong on military matters shows distinctive insight. Have you long devoted your attention to civil affairs and military preparedness? Selected, you will surely prove a useful talent.
Associate Examiner Liu, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi), comments: Sacrificial regulations and military administration concern great affairs of state and must be thoroughly examined. Candidates in the examination hall mostly repeat stale pronouncements and have no settled views. You alone investigate thoroughly and clearly, weighing the alternatives with fitting judgment in every detail. You possess outstanding talent for statecraft, beyond comparison with those who merely display ornate language. Let this essay be recorded and presented, to help settle national policy.
Examiner Shen, a Hanlin Academy Compiler, comments: Opinions differ on associated sacrifices and the capital garrisons. You reconcile the many doubts and explain each point as clearly as if pointing to your palm. Your broad learning and far-reaching insight are beyond the attainment of shallow scholars. This essay should be recorded as a model.
Examiner Ding, Right Admonisher, comments: This essay answers the questions on sacrifices and military affairs point by point, analyzing the various views and arriving at the most fitting conclusions. Its closing passage is especially earnest about the difficulties of deliberating on ritual and changing established institutions. Its author is surely a mature man of foresight. Can he be regarded merely as a student of the Classics? Highly recommended, highly recommended!
You, honored examiners, have condescended to question us students about the rites of associated sacrifice and the organization of the capital garrisons. Do you suppose that even humble woodcutters and grass gatherers may have some part in deliberations on the great plans of the court? I, in my ignorance, am not such a person. Ritual has five principal divisions, of which none is weightier than sacrifice. Great indeed is the significance of sacrifice; and investigating and determining who should receive associated sacrifices is an especially weighty matter within the sacrificial regulations. Can it be discussed lightly? Heaven produced the five materials; who can…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
去兵兵之爲用大矣而更革營制尤戎務
之大者也可輕議哉雖然籩豆之事儒者
之所嘗聞軍旅之事有國者之所不廢執
事之問不敢虛也請就正焉以從祀言之
我
太祖之始定天下也首建學校親祠孔子而從
祀諸賢則因唐開元之舊焉當其時嘗罷
孟子之配享矣而旋議復之嘗因言者之
請而黜揚雄矣於董子則進之此從祀之
===
始議也崇德報功真得勵世淑人之機矣
時尚倥偬有未暇致詳者自是以來各有
論列而議者始紛然焉卒未有折群疑而
歸於正者也我
世宗肅皇帝際治教之休明也議禮考文
特加增定維時撤虛位者一人則申黨是也
增入祀者五人則后蒼王通諸人是也黜
從祀者一十三人則公伯寮秦冉顏何諸
人是也罷從祀而祀於其鄉者七人則林

去兵？兵之爲用大矣，而更革營制尤戎務之大者也，可輕議哉？雖然，籩豆之事，儒者之所嘗聞；軍旅之事，有國者之所不廢。執事之問，不敢虛也，請就正焉。
以從祀言之，我太祖之始定天下也，首建學校，親祠孔子，而從祀諸賢則因唐開元之舊焉。當其時，嘗罷孟子之配享矣，而旋議復之；嘗因言者之請而黜揚雄矣，於董子則進之。此從祀之始議也。崇德報功，真得勵世淑人之機矣。時尚倥偬，有未暇致詳者。自是以來，各有論列，而議者始紛然焉，卒未有折群疑而歸於正者也。
我世宗肅皇帝際治教之休明也，議禮考文，特加增定。維時撤虛位者一人，則申黨是也；增入祀者五人，則后蒼、王通諸人是也；黜從祀者一十三人，則公伯寮、秦冉、顏何諸人是也；罷從祀而祀於其鄉者七人，則林
translation_en:
…dispense with arms? The use of arms is a matter of great consequence, and reforming the military camp organization is an especially weighty matter of military administration. Can it be discussed lightly? Nevertheless, matters of sacrificial vessels are familiar to Confucian scholars, while military affairs cannot be neglected by those who govern a state. I dare not leave your questions unanswered; allow me to submit my views for your correction.
To speak of subsidiary worship in the Confucian temple: when our Emperor Taizu first pacified the realm, he made establishing schools his foremost concern and personally offered sacrifices to Kongzi. As for the worthies receiving subsidiary worship, he followed the precedents of the Kaiyuan era of the Tang. At that time, he once discontinued Mengzi’s associate sacrifice, but soon deliberated on restoring it. He also excluded Yang Xiong at the request of a remonstrant, while admitting Master Dong. These were the first deliberations on subsidiary worship. In honoring virtue and requiting merit, they truly grasped the means of inspiring the age and improving its people. Yet affairs were still unsettled, and there were details for which time had not permitted full consideration. Thereafter, various proposals were submitted, and opinions began to proliferate. Ultimately, no one resolved the many doubts and brought the matter into accord with what was right.
Our Emperor Shizong, posthumously honored as Su, in an age of flourishing government and moral instruction, deliberated on ritual and examined cultural institutions, giving particular attention to additions and revisions. At that time, one person’s unwarranted spirit tablet was removed: Shen Dang. Five people were newly admitted to worship, including Hou Cang and Wang Tong. Thirteen were excluded from subsidiary worship, including Gongbo Liao, Qin Ran, and Yan He. Seven ceased to receive subsidiary worship but were instead worshipped in their native places, including Lin…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
放蘧瑗鄭衆諸人是也盖有其舉之而非
以尚同也有其廢之而非以立異也禮正
百王考諸前而不謬識高千古俟諸後而
不惑所謂進退古今
世宗以之執事以為無容喙焉不信然乎邇者
建言諸臣又有議舉議復至欲舉當代薛
王二臣從祀者則固有說也夫我
明興二百餘年絃歌之化達乎遐邇三尺童
子皆知誦法孔氏而璧宮之側至今無一
===
人俎豆其間豈所以鼓士氣而彰
聖朝棫樸之盛也哉此闡揚潜德固言官之大
節也顧今
詔集群議且有日矣而應議之臣卒持之而
莫有定者盖緣建言者有見於祀典之不
可以或遺而掌禮者有見於祀典之不容
以或濫是以心心有主莫之統同耳議禮
之家勢則然也何嫌其為異哉乃若至當
歸一之論則誠不必師心以自是而貴于

可以或遺而掌禮者有見於祀典之不容
以或濫是以心心有主莫之統同耳議禮
之家勢則然也何嫌其爲異哉乃若至當

punctuated:
放、蘧瑗、鄭衆諸人是也。盖有其舉之，而非以尚同也；有其廢之，而非以立異也。禮正百王，考諸前而不謬；識高千古，俟諸後而不惑。所謂進退古今，世宗以之。執事以為無容喙焉，不信然乎？邇者建言諸臣，又有議舉、議復，至欲舉當代薛、王二臣從祀者，則固有說也。夫我明興二百餘年，絃歌之化達乎遐邇，三尺童子皆知誦法孔氏，而璧宮之側，至今無一人俎豆其間，豈所以鼓士氣而彰聖朝棫樸之盛也哉？此闡揚潜德，固言官之大節也。
顧今詔集群議，且有日矣，而應議之臣卒持之而莫有定者，盖緣建言者有見於祀典之不可以或遺，而掌禮者有見於祀典之不容以或濫，是以心心有主，莫之統同耳。議禮之家，勢則然也，何嫌其為異哉？乃若至當歸一之論，則誠不必師心以自是，而貴于
translation_en:
… Lin Fang, Qu Yuan, Zheng Zhong, and others were such men. Some were elevated, but not for the sake of conformity; some were removed, but not for the sake of asserting a difference. His ritual judgments set right those of the hundred kings: tested against the past, they were without error. His discernment surpassed that of a thousand ages: awaiting the judgment of posterity, it would admit no doubt. What is called advancing or retiring men of past and present—Shizong put this into practice. You hold that there is no room for further comment: is this not indeed so? Recently, ministers submitting proposals have again advocated admitting some men and restoring others, even wishing to admit the two ministers of our own dynasty, Xue and Wang, to accompanying worship in the Confucian temple. There are certainly grounds for this. More than two hundred years have passed since our Ming arose. The civilizing influence of strings and song has reached both near and far; even little children know to recite Confucius’s teachings and take him as their model. Yet beside the imperial school, to this day not one man of our dynasty receives sacrificial offerings. How can this encourage the spirit of scholars and display our sagely dynasty’s flourishing cultivation of worthy men, celebrated in the ode “Yu pu” (“The Oak Trees”)? Bringing hidden virtue to light is certainly a major duty of remonstrance officials.
Yet some time has now passed since an imperial edict called for opinions to be gathered, and the ministers charged with deliberation still cling to their positions without reaching a decision. This is because those making proposals recognize that the sacrificial canon must omit no one who belongs in it, while those administering rites recognize that it must admit no one indiscriminately. Each mind thus has its own settled position, and no one brings them into agreement. Among those who deliberate on ritual, such a situation is natural. Why object to their differences? As for a judgment that is supremely fitting and commands agreement, one certainly need not take one’s own mind as the sole authority and insist upon one’s own correctness; rather, what is to be valued is …

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
好問以用中焉何也禮以義起不協于義則
不可以爲禮也禮緣人情不近人情不可以
以爲禮也夫蘧瑗林放非及門之士也祀
瑗於衞祀放於魯於義協矣於情近矣矧
先帝嘗正之哉莫敢舉也羅從彦李侗明聖人
之道者也登之俎豆列之尸祝於義協矣
於情近矣
先帝特未之舉耳從祀可也盖羅李之正學固
淵源於伊洛者惡得少其著述而致疑之
===
哉若文清之祀所當先舉者焉何也世代
則已遠公論固已著也新建之祀所當徐
議者焉何也世代則稍近公論猶未定也
盖後之視王必有如今之視薛者惡得比
而同之而槩莫之舉哉此議從祀者之大
較也以營制言之我
高皇之定鼎金陵也於五軍將士始立大小教
塲以訓練之迨我
文皇之考卜燕京也既有五軍營矣又有三千

punctuated:
好問以用中焉。何也？禮以義起，不協于義，則不可以爲禮也。禮緣人情，不近人情，不可以以爲禮也。夫蘧瑗、林放，非及門之士也。祀瑗於衞，祀放於魯，於義協矣，於情近矣。矧先帝嘗正之哉！莫敢舉也。羅從彦、李侗，明聖人之道者也。登之俎豆，列之尸祝，於義協矣，於情近矣。先帝特未之舉耳，從祀可也。盖羅、李之正學，固淵源於伊洛者，惡得少其著述而致疑之哉！若文清之祀，所當先舉者焉。何也？世代則已遠，公論固已著也。新建之祀，所當徐議者焉。何也？世代則稍近，公論猶未定也。盖後之視王，必有如今之視薛者，惡得比而同之，而槩莫之舉哉！此議從祀者之大較也。

以營制言之，我高皇之定鼎金陵也，於五軍將士，始立大小教塲以訓練之。迨我文皇之考卜燕京也，既有五軍營矣，又有三千
translation_en:
…to delight in inquiry and thereby apply the mean. Why? Ritual arises from righteousness: what does not accord with righteousness cannot constitute ritual. Ritual follows human feelings: what does not accord with human feelings cannot constitute ritual. Qu Yuan 蘧瑗 and Lin Fang were not disciples who had studied directly under the Sage. Sacrificing to Qu Yuan in Wei and to Lin Fang in Lu accords with righteousness and accords with human feelings. Moreover, the late emperor already rectified this matter! No one dares propose [a change?]. Luo Congyan and Li Tong elucidated the Way of the Sage. To offer them sacrifices and include them among those honored in sacrificial rites accords with righteousness and accords with human feelings. The late emperor simply had not undertaken this; admitting them to associated worship in the Confucian temple is permissible. The orthodox learning of Luo and Li certainly derived from the Yi–Luo tradition. How could one cast doubt on them because their writings were few?

As for sacrifices to Wenqing [Xue Xuan], these should be instituted first. Why? His time is already distant, and public judgment has long been clear. Sacrifices to Xinjian [Wang Shouren] should be deliberated more slowly. Why? His time is relatively recent, and public judgment remains unsettled. Surely later generations will regard Wang as people today regard Xue. How could one place them on the same footing and institute sacrifices to neither? These are the broad considerations governing discussion of associated worship.

Turning to the organization of military camps: when our Emperor Gao established his capital at Jinling, he first set up large and small drill grounds to train the officers and soldiers of the Five Armies. When our Emperor Wen selected Yanjing as his capital, there was already the Five Armies Camp, and there was also the Three Thousand …

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
神機二營以附之因稱三大營焉此營制
之所自始也
神謀睿算真得乎居重馭輕之道矣是宜世
守之而不變者沿至于後則代有增置寖
失
聖祖之制焉無惑乎其將愈多而兵愈弱也至
我
世宗肅皇帝憤醜虜之犯順也張皇六師
特修戎政維時遵復
===
祖制仍五軍神機之舊易三千曰神樞為三大
營焉又為開府命大將督之而以兵曹卿
貳協理之又各營有副參遊佐及練勇諸
將以分領操練之事而咸統於大將焉是
其神樞之易名十二營之更革諸將佐之
兼設戎政府之特建雖出於通變神化之
宜而三大營之制則所以復
聖祖之舊也故居常則嚴捍衛而內足以固
京師有警則聽征調而外足以懾奸宄所謂

punctuated: 神機二營以附之，因稱三大營焉。此營制之所自始也。神謀睿算，真得乎居重馭輕之道矣！是宜世守之而不變者。沿至于後，則代有增置，寖失聖祖之制焉。無惑乎其將愈多而兵愈弱也。至我世宗肅皇帝憤醜虜之犯順也，張皇六師，特修戎政。維時遵復祖制，仍五軍、神機之舊，易三千曰神樞，為三大營焉。又為開府，命大將督之，而以兵曹卿貳協理之。又各營有副、參、遊、佐及練勇諸將，以分領操練之事，而咸統於大將焉。是其神樞之易名、十二營之更革、諸將佐之兼設、戎政府之特建，雖出於通變神化之宜，而三大營之制，則所以復聖祖之舊也。故居常則嚴捍衛，而內足以固京師；有警則聽征調，而外足以懾奸宄。所謂
translation_en:
…the two camps, Sanqian (Three Thousand) and Shenji (Divine Mechanism), were attached to it, and together they were therefore called the Three Great Camps. This was the origin of the camp system. Such divine planning and sagacious calculation truly grasped the principle of concentrating strength at the center to control the less powerful periphery! This was a system that ought to have been preserved unchanged for generations. Subsequently, however, successive reigns added establishments, gradually departing from the sacred ancestor’s system. No wonder that the more numerous the commanders became, the weaker the troops grew.

When our Emperor Shizong, posthumously honored as Su, became indignant at the vile barbarians’ violation of the lawful order, he strengthened the Six Armies and undertook a special reform of military administration. At that time, he restored the ancestral system, retaining the old Wujun (Five Armies) and Shenji camps and renaming Sanqian as Shenshu (Divine Pivot), thus constituting the Three Great Camps. He also established a headquarters, appointing a general to command them and assigning the Minister and Vice Ministers of War to assist in their administration. Each camp also had deputy regional commanders, assistant regional commanders, mobile corps commanders, assistant officers, and commanders responsible for training picked troops. They divided responsibility for drills and training, but all came under the general’s command.

Thus, the renaming of Shenshu, the reorganization of the Twelve Camps, the concurrent appointment of commanders and their assistants, and the special establishment of the military administration headquarters were measures suited to adapting to change with consummate ingenuity; yet the system of Three Great Camps served to restore the sacred ancestor’s former arrangements. In ordinary times they maintained strict protection, providing sufficient strength within to secure the capital; when an alarm arose, they obeyed orders for mobilization, providing sufficient strength beyond the capital to overawe evildoers. This is what is meant by…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
善繼善述
世宗以之執事以爲詳慎不其然乎邇者輔弼
之臣又有議遵
祖制收兵權以飭戎務者則誠有見也夫我
國家奠鼎燕京密邇强虜所隔者僅山後耳
乃士馬消耗將領巽懦若是有國家長遠
之慮者能不爲之寒心哉此計安社稷固
輔臣之忠猷也廼今
成命已頒戎制定矣而當事諸臣統紀漫無
===
定執者蓋緣經國者知兵權之不可不收
而督戎者謂事權之不可不一是以此甲
彼乙不能相統耳變法之難理則然也何
害其爲同哉乃若轉弱爲强之道則誠不
在於營制之參伍而在於御將士之有律
焉蓋御得其道則營制伍焉可也參焉亦
可也御失其道則營制參焉無裨也伍焉
亦無裨也誠於御將也制其功罪而不爲
姑息則將雖强必戢許以便宜而不從中

punctuated: 善繼善述，世宗以之。執事以爲詳慎，不其然乎？邇者，輔弼之臣又有議遵祖制、收兵權以飭戎務者，則誠有見也。夫我國家奠鼎燕京，密邇强虜，所隔者僅山後耳。乃士馬消耗，將領巽懦若是，有國家長遠之慮者，能不爲之寒心哉？此計安社稷，固輔臣之忠猷也。廼今成命已頒，戎制定矣，而當事諸臣統紀漫無定執者，蓋緣經國者知兵權之不可不收，而督戎者謂事權之不可不一，是以此甲彼乙，不能相統耳。變法之難，理則然也，何害其爲同哉？乃若轉弱爲强之道，則誠不在於營制之參伍，而在於御將士之有律焉。蓋御得其道，則營制伍焉可也，參焉亦可也；御失其道，則營制參焉無裨也，伍焉亦無裨也。誠於御將也，制其功罪而不爲姑息，則將雖强必戢；許以便宜而不從中
translation_en:
…skillfully carrying forward and fulfilling his predecessors’ purposes: Shizong put this into practice. You regard this as thorough and prudent—is that not so? Recently, ministers assisting the throne have also proposed following the ancestral institutions and gathering military authority back into central hands to put military affairs in order. This indeed shows insight. Our dynasty established its capital at Yanjing, very near the powerful northern enemy, with only the region beyond the mountains separating us. Yet our men and horses are depleted, and our commanders are so timid and weak. Could anyone concerned for the dynasty’s long-term future fail to be chilled at heart? This plan to secure the altars of soil and grain is certainly a loyal proposal by the assisting ministers.

Now the imperial command has been issued and the military organization settled. Yet the responsible ministers still have no firmly established principles of command and discipline. This is because those administering the state recognize that military authority must be gathered into central hands, while those directing military affairs maintain that operational authority must be unified. Thus one advocates one course and another a different one, and they cannot coordinate their authority. Such difficulties in changing institutions are natural; why should they prevent agreement? As for the way to turn weakness into strength, it truly lies not in whether the camps are organized into three or five divisions, but in governing commanders and soldiers with discipline. If they are governed properly, an organization of five camps will do, and so will three. If they are governed improperly, three camps will be of no benefit, and neither will five.

If, in governing commanders, one truly regulates rewards and punishments for their merits and offenses without indulging them, even overbearing commanders will restrain themselves. If one permits them to act as circumstances require and does not, from the court …

寡矣何也事權一也不然雖韓白其朋秪

者寡矣何也法守一也不然雖貔貅如林

===

而知
祖宗之憲章有不容以輕議者宋祖親賛孔顏
祀典既定矣迨其後也至有欲退孟軻而
進安石又欲躋之於尼父者此何說也彼

此耳唐宗創立府兵兵制已定矣迨其後
也至變為彍騎變為藩鎮而終為唐室梗
者此何說也彼盖輕議祖宗之兵制而不

translation_en:
…restrain them from the center, then even weak generals will surely exert themselves. In this way there will be little cause to fear a failure to rally. Why? Because authority over affairs is unified. Otherwise, even if their ranks included Han Xin and Bai Qi, they would merely contend for precedence in ceremonial formalities and obstruct one another over differences of opinion. What benefit would there be in changing military institutions every day? In managing the soldiers, investigate their assignment to service [?] and punish omissions and evasions: then even a small force will serve as a large one. Select the best and bravest and train them methodically: then even weak soldiers will become strong. In this way there will be little cause to fear timidity and weakness. Why? Because the rules they observe are uniform. Otherwise, even if fierce warriors stood as thick as a forest, they would merely swarm like ants at the office that distributes provisions and submit to commands issued with a nod at the military authorities’ gates. What benefit would there be in changing military institutions every month? These are the broad considerations for those discussing the organization of military camps.
Nevertheless, this humble student has also learned something further. Having repeatedly examined the affairs of the Tang and Song, I understand that the ancestral emperors’ established institutions cannot be lightly called into question. The founding emperor of the Song personally composed praises of Kongzi and Yan Hui, and the sacrificial regulations were already settled. Yet later there were those who wished to demote Meng Ke and elevate Wang Anshi, and even to raise the latter to the rank of Master Kong. How can this be explained? They lightly questioned the ancestral emperors’ sacrificial regulations and thus unwittingly allowed their deterioration to reach this point. The Tang emperor established the militia system known as fubing, and the military institutions were already settled. Yet later these were transformed into the expanded cavalry, or guoqi, and then into regional military commands, which ultimately became a scourge of the Tang ruling house. How can this be explained? translation_en:
…realize that a single rash step had brought matters to this pass. Should those who now discuss sacrifices and military affairs not therefore exercise caution? When the former minister Song Lian discussed temple sacrifices, he said: “Confucius brought together the great achievements of all the sages, and the Four Masters transmitted Confucius’s succession of the Way. It is fitting that they should receive sacrifices throughout the realm. As for the others, each region should honor its own former worthies. Even the sacrifices to the seventy-two disciples should be discontinued and instead established at the National University. This would come close to avoiding any violation of ritual propriety.” How true these words are! They can serve as a standard for those discussing associated worship in the Confucian temple. Why must they clamor and dispute day after day?

When our Emperor Shizong instructed the Minister of War, his decree read: “The affairs of the capital garrisons are no small matter. Only by restoring the ancestral institutions can authority be unified, crack troops maintained, and practical needs met. Abolish all the designations of the Twelve Garrisons and the Two Command Offices.” How great are these imperial words! They can serve as a guide for those discussing the organization of the garrisons. Why must they busy themselves in a flurry of institutional changes?

Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

His Majesty studies antiquity and esteems letters, summons worthy men and honors the Lord on High, establishing the foremost example of good government beginning with the capital. In the gengwu year of Longqing [1570], when the triennial examination of scholars was due, an imperial edict specially approved the proposal of the scholarly officials to increase the provincial graduate quotas of the two capitals. Your servants Shimei and Shixing were duly commanded to oversee the Shuntian examination. When the record was completed, it fell to your servant Shixing to append a postface to its final pages.

I humbly reflect that, some years ago, I served as an Associate Examiner at the Metropolitan Examination. 從事，可不謂奇遘乎？非獨臣爾，卽諸士所遘，臣亦奇之。
國家設科斂材，著爲令式，儒生斌斌向盛矣。有司謹奉繩墨，毎賓興士，如約而止，士不能無留良焉。臣方祗事國史，閱先朝所上章牘，諸請益解士者，輒報聞罷。故自儒臣始上議，衆猶睢睢盱盱，竊相謂難之。而皇上霈然發德音，幸而聽許，一時縉紳章縫靡不神竦色澤，竊嘆聖天子振世作人，嘉惠賢雋，前此
translation_en:
…to take part in this undertaking—can this not be called an extraordinary encounter? Nor is this true of your servant alone: I also marvel at the opportunity that these scholars have encountered.
The state established examinations to gather talent and enshrined them in its regulations. Cultivated scholars have flourished in increasing numbers. The responsible officials scrupulously observe the prescribed rules; whenever they select scholars for advancement, they stop at the stipulated quota, inevitably leaving some worthy men unselected. Your servant is currently reverently engaged in compiling the national history. In reading memorials submitted during previous reigns, I have found that requests to increase the number of provincial graduates were invariably acknowledged and then dismissed. Thus, when the scholarly officials first submitted this proposal, people still looked about apprehensively, privately telling one another how difficult it would be to secure approval. Yet His Majesty graciously issued his benevolent pronouncement and, fortunately, consented. At once, officials and scholars alike were stirred in spirit, their faces radiant. They privately exclaimed that the sagely Son of Heaven was invigorating the age and nurturing talent, graciously bestowing favor upon the worthy and outstanding, and that before this…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
未有也乃諸士生
畿輔游辟雝適會其時臣故曰
竒遘也夫非常之恩所以待
非常之材國士遇則國士報
今臣所爲報
上在得士耳而士直懷鉛抱槧以
文詞進安所得非常之材而
===
信之然臣聞楚相髙梱而民
無庳車齊王朝而惡紫國人
莫衣紫從所好也故
上意有嚮則化捷風行聲疾雷震
天下赴之如影響而從之如
流矧都人士皆燕趙間材古
所稱慷慨沈毅懷節義幹者

文詞進安所得非常之材而
===
信之然臣聞楚相高拐而民
無庳車齊王朝而惡紫國人
莫衣紫從所好也故
上意有嚮則化捷風行聲疾雷震
天下赴之如影響而從之如
流矧都人士皆燕趙間材古
所稱慷慨沈毅懷節義幹者
punctuated: 未有也。乃諸士生畿輔，游辟雝，適會其時，臣故曰竒遘也。夫非常之恩，所以待非常之材；國士遇，則國士報。今臣所爲報上，在得士耳。而士直懷鉛抱槧，以文詞進，安所得非常之材而信之？然臣聞楚相髙梱，而民無庳車；齊王朝而惡紫，國人莫衣紫，從所好也。故上意有嚮，則化捷風行，聲疾雷震；天下赴之如影響，而從之如流。矧都人士皆燕趙間材，古所稱慷慨沈毅、懷節義幹者，
translation_en:
…had never occurred before. These scholars, born in the metropolitan region and studying in the imperial academy, have happened upon precisely this moment. Your servant therefore calls it a rare encounter. Extraordinary favor is bestowed in expectation of extraordinary talent; those treated as outstanding men of the realm will repay that treatment as outstanding men of the realm. My own means of repaying Your Majesty now lies solely in finding worthy scholars. Yet if scholars merely carry lead writing implements and wooden tablets and seek advancement through literary composition, how can I find men of extraordinary talent and be confident of their worth?

Yet I have heard that the chief minister of Chu raised the thresholds [?], and the people had no low carriages; the king of Qi expressed his dislike of purple at court, and no one in the state wore purple. They followed the preferences of those above them. Thus, when the imperial will inclines in a particular direction, its transforming influence spreads swiftly as the wind, and its voice resounds rapidly as thunder. All under Heaven hasten toward it as shadows and echoes respond, and follow it like flowing water. How much more so the scholars of the capital, all talented men from the region of Yan and Zhao, whom the ancients described as spirited and resolute, steadfast and possessed of integrity, righteousness, and ability…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
士從四方来固遊燕趙間者
也又皆沾被
德澤躡明昌之期寧無負非常之
材抱國士之素爭自磨濯以
對揚
休命者乎茲者臣校其文大都說
稱先王指事陳世能激昂持
===
論不卑卑為謏聞陋儒則庶
幾哉材亦有竒足以答此竒
遘臣所為藉手報
上彰
國家得人之盛者將無是賴乎
顧臣復有言焉古稱得人盛
者以才小大不以衆寡盖孔

顧臣復有言焉：古稱得人盛者，以才小大，不以衆寡。盖孔
translation_en:
…The scholars come from all quarters and indeed sojourn in the lands of Yan and Zhao. All, moreover, have received the blessings of imperial virtue and entered an age of enlightened prosperity. Could there be none among them who possess extraordinary talents and the qualities of an outstanding servant of the state, striving to refine and cleanse themselves so as to acknowledge and extol the gracious command? In examining their writings on this occasion, your servant has found that most invoke the former kings, address particular affairs, and discuss the conditions of the age. They advance their arguments with spirit, rather than abasing themselves as ill-informed, narrow-minded scholars. They thus come close to what is hoped for! Among their talents are exceptional ones, sufficient to answer this exceptional opportunity. Might not your servant rely upon these as the means to repay His Majesty and display the state's flourishing success in obtaining worthy men?
Yet your servant has something further to say. When the ancients spoke of flourishing success in obtaining worthy men, they judged by the magnitude of their talents, not by their numbers. For Confucius…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
子稱唐虞成周夫唐虞五臣
周九人止矣而號棊隆漢以
下圖形書帛推轂標榜多不
可勝數然不逮古遠矣故士
誠傑材雖寡盛也如取充而
已雖衆不爲盛以其無當于
大受也邇者海内有急𢙢𢙢稱
乏材至令人人論薦章交公
車矣
聖天子取士如故法
恩渥有加焉猶尚如是則臣竊愧
之今諸士增增貢籍誠得傑
士如臣言異日足稱任使副
德意則信盛矣設今日所舉不必

translation_en:
…Confucius praised the ages of Tang and Yu and the Zhou dynasty in its formative period. Tang and Yu had five ministers, and Zhou only nine, yet their renown was exalted [?]. From the Han onward, those whose portraits were painted and whose deeds were recorded on silk, who were recommended and publicly acclaimed, were too numerous to count; nevertheless, they fell far short of antiquity. Thus, if scholars truly possess outstanding talent, even a few constitute an abundance. If they are merely selected to fill the numbers, even a multitude does not constitute an abundance, for they are unequal to great responsibilities.

Recently, when emergencies arose within the realm, there were anxious cries of a shortage of talent, to the point that everyone was ordered to discuss and recommend candidates, and memorials poured into the office receiving submissions to the throne. The sagely Son of Heaven selects scholars according to the established rules, bestowing still greater favor upon them. That matters should nevertheless remain thus makes your servant privately ashamed.

Now these scholars swell the registers of those presented to the court [?]. If we have truly obtained outstanding scholars of the kind your servant describes, who in days to come will prove equal to their appointments and duties and fulfill Your Majesty’s benevolent intentions, then this will indeed be an abundance of talent. If, however, those recommended today are not necessarily…

title: 隆慶四年順天府鄉試錄
text:
賢于疇昔或又弗逮令
廟堂憂乏材無已時則安用此多
士為哉夫實不中其聲窺言
也梯榮階進苟志利祿穻心
也已獲嚮用舉生平而弁髦
之釋行也有一于此則臣過
信諸士而諸士乃大謬不然
===
是臣以非材進耳夫安所逃
責矣詩曰王國克生維周之
楨書曰稱匪其人惟爾不任
諸士尚思為王國之楨母使
臣蒙不任之臯哉
翰林院修撰儒林郎申時行
謹序

是臣以非材進耳夫安所逃
責矣詩曰王國克生維周之
楨書曰稱匪其人惟爾不任
諸士尚思爲王國之楨毋使
臣蒙不任之辠哉
翰林院修撰儒林郎申時行
謹序
punctuated:
賢于疇昔，或又弗逮，令廟堂憂乏材無已時，則安用此多士為哉？夫實不中其聲，窺言也；梯榮階進，苟志利祿，穻心也；已獲嚮用，舉生平而弁髦之，釋行也。有一于此，則臣過信諸士，而諸士乃大謬。不然，是臣以非材進耳，夫安所逃責矣？《詩》曰：「王國克生，維周之楨。」《書》曰：「稱匪其人，惟爾不任。」諸士尚思為王國之楨，母使臣蒙不任之臯哉！
翰林院修撰儒林郎申時行謹序。
translation_en:
…more worthy than those of former days, or perhaps even inferior to them, causing the court to worry endlessly about a shortage of talent—then what use would this multitude of scholars be? If their actual qualities do not match their reputation, theirs is hollow speech [?]; if they climb toward honors and advance through the ranks, intent merely on profit and official emoluments, theirs is a base purpose [?]; if, once favored with employment, they cast aside all their lifelong principles like a discarded ceremonial cap and hairpiece, they abandon proper conduct. If any one of these failings occurs, then I have trusted these scholars too readily, and they have gone gravely astray. Otherwise, it is I who have recommended men without talent. How could I escape responsibility?

The Book of Odes says: “The royal kingdom can bring forth men who are the pillars of Zhou.” The Book of Documents says: “If those you recommend are not the right men, it is you who are unfit for your charge.” May you scholars aspire to be pillars of the royal kingdom, and not cause me to incur the blame [?] of being unfit for my charge!

Preface respectfully composed by Shen Shixing, Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy, Gentleman of Scholarly Service.
